content: 1. The co-administration of antacids with rilpivirine can significantly reduce rilpivirine plasma concentrations due to an increase in gastric pH. If antacids must be used, they should be administered at least 2 hours before or at least 4 hours after rilpivirine. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 2. Magnesium oxide decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction is specific to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be adjusted or monitored closely. 3. For the combination product dolutegravir/rilpivirine, antacids should be administered at least 4 hours before or at least 6 hours after the combination. Close monitoring is required. 4. Magnesium sulfate decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 5. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of maprotiline by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Rilpivirine should be used cautiously when co-administered with drugs that have a known risk of Torsade de Pointes. 6. Mavorixafor increases rilpivirine levels or effects by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Both mavorixafor and rilpivirine prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Mavorixafor causes concentration-dependent QTc prolongation, and QTc should be monitored during treatment in patients with risk factors for QTc prolongation. Dose reduction or discontinuation of mavorixafor may be required. 7. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of mefloquine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Rilpivirine should be used cautiously when co-administered with drugs that have a known risk of Torsade de Pointes. 8. No dose adjustments are required when initiating co-administration of methadone with rilpivirine. However, rilpivirine increases the toxicity of methadone by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Rilpivirine should be used cautiously when co-administered with drugs that have a known risk of Torsade de Pointes. 9. Mirtazapine and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Moxifloxacin increases the toxicity of rilpivirine by prolonging the QTc interval, and rilpivirine increases the toxicity of moxifloxacin by the same mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Rilpivirine should be used cautiously when co-administered with drugs that have a known risk of Torsade de Pointes. 11. Nefazodone increases rilpivirine levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Nelfinavir increases rilpivirine levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Nevirapine decreases rilpivirine levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Rilpivirine should not be used in combination with NNRTIs. 14. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of nilotinib by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Rilpivirine should be used cautiously when co-administered with drugs that have a known risk of Torsade de Pointes. 15. Nizatidine decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Concurrent use may lead to treatment failure and/or the development of rilpivirine or NNRTI resistance. Administer H2 antagonists at least 12 hours before or at least 4 hours after rilpivirine. 16. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of nortriptyline by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Rilpivirine should be used cautiously when co-administered with drugs that have a known risk of Torsade de Pointes. 17. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of octreotide by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Rilpivirine should be used cautiously when co-administered with drugs that have a known risk of Torsade de Pointes. 18. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of ofloxacin by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Rilpivirine should be used cautiously when co-administered with drugs that have a known risk of Torsade de Pointes. 19. Olanzapine and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir and dasabuvir (DSC) increase rilpivirine levels or effects by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration of Viekira Pak with rilpivirine once daily is not recommended due to the potential for QT interval prolongation with higher rilpivirine concentrations. 21. Omeprazole decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. This combination is contraindicated. Concurrent use may lead to treatment failure and/or the development of rilpivirine or NNRTI resistance. 22. Orlistat decreases rilpivirine levels or effects by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Loss of virological control has been reported in HIV-infected patients taking orlistat concomitantly. The exact mechanism is unclear but may involve a drug-drug interaction that inhibits systemic absorption of the antiretroviral drug. Monitor HIV RNA levels frequently, and if increased HIV viral load is confirmed, discontinue orlistat. 23. Osilodrostat and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Oxaliplatin and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 25. Oxcarbazepine decreases rilpivirine levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Rilpivirine should not be co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inducers due to the potential for loss of virologic response and possible resistance to rilpivirine or the NNRTI class. 26. Phenytoin decreases rilpivirine levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Rilpivirine should not be co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inducers due to the potential for loss of virologic response and possible resistance to rilpivirine or the NNRTI class. 27. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of pimozide by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Rilpivirine should be used cautiously when co-administered with drugs that have a known risk of Torsade de Pointes. 28. Posaconazole increases rilpivirine levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. No rilpivirine dose adjustment is required. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of posaconazole by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Potassium chloride decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. If antacids must be administered, they should be given at least 2 hours before or at least 4 hours after rilpivirine. 30. Primaquine and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of procainamide by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Rilpivirine should be used cautiously when co-administered with drugs that have a known risk of Torsade de Pointes. 32. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of propafenone by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Rilpivirine should be used cautiously when co-administered with drugs that have a known risk of Torsade de Pointes. 33. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of protriptyline by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Rilpivirine should be used cautiously when co-administered with drugs that have a known risk of Torsade de Pointes. 34. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of quetiapine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Rilpivirine should be used cautiously when co-administered with drugs that have a known risk of Torsade de Pointes. 35. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of quinidine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Rilpivirine should be used cautiously when co-administered with drugs that have a known risk of Torsade de Pointes. 36. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of quinine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Rilpivirine should be used cautiously when co-administered with drugs that have a known risk of Torsade de Pointes. 37. Quizartinib and rilpivirine both increase the effects of the other by prolonging the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Patients should be monitored more frequently with ECG if co-administered with QT-prolonging drugs. 38. Rabeprazole decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. This combination is contraindicated. Concurrent use may lead to treatment failure and/or the development of rilpivirine or NNRTI resistance. 39. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of ranolazine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Rilpivirine should be used cautiously when co-administered with drugs that have a known risk of Torsade de Pointes. 40. Ribociclib increases the toxicity of rilpivirine by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 41. Rifabutin decreases rilpivirine levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administered, increase rilpivirine dose to 50 mg orally once daily. When rifabutin co-administration is stopped, decrease rilpivirine dose to 25 mg once daily. 42. Rifampin decreases rilpivirine levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Rilpivirine should not be co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inducers due to the potential for loss of virologic response and possible resistance to rilpivirine or the NNRTI class. 43. Rifapentine decreases rilpivirine levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Rilpivirine should not be co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inducers due to the potential for loss of virologic response and possible resistance to rilpivirine or the NNRTI class. 44. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of risperidone by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Rilpivirine should be used cautiously when co-administered with drugs that have a known risk of Torsade de Pointes. 45. Ritonavir increases rilpivirine levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of ritonavir by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of romidepsin by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Rilpivirine should be used cautiously when co-administered with drugs that have a known risk of Torsade de Pointes. 47. Selpercatinib increases the toxicity of rilpivirine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Sertraline and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Sevoflurane and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 50. Siponimod and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 51. Sodium zirconium cyclosilicate decreases rilpivirine levels or effects by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Drugs with pH-dependent solubility that may affect systemic exposure and efficacy should be administered at least 2 hours before or after sodium zirconium cyclosilicate. 52. Solifenacin and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of sotalol by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Rilpivirine should be used cautiously when co-administered with drugs that have a known risk of Torsade de Pointes. 54. St. John’s Wort decreases rilpivirine levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Rilpivirine should not be co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inducers due to the potential for loss of virologic response and possible resistance to rilpivirine or the NNRTI class.
